title: Post-9/11 GI Bill Tuition and Fees Paid to Schools
content:
**Desk guidance — tuition and fees under Education Benefits (GI Bill and Dependents' Education).**

**Rule.** Post-9/11 GI Bill tuition and fees are paid directly to the school once per certified term. At a public school the actual net in-state tuition and fees are covered without a dollar cap; at a private or foreign school the payment for an academic year is limited to the private and foreign school annual cap of the tier; in either case the result is multiplied by the benefit level of the tier and kept to the cent. Tuition above the cap at a private school can be partly covered by Yellow Ribbon matching only where the tier is eligible for Yellow Ribbon and the school has a Yellow Ribbon agreement covering the student's program. Flat-rate chapters never pay tuition to the school.

**Condition.** Tuition is paid only for a certification on a benefit whose status is active. The status is read from the benefit record that the certification uses, before payment; an exhausted, delimited or relinquished benefit does not qualify.

**Condition — result table**

| Benefit status on the certification's benefit | School type | Amount paid to the school |
|---|---|---|
| Active | Public | Net in-state tuition and fees charged, multiplied by the benefit level |
| Active | Private or foreign | Tuition and fees charged up to the annual cap, multiplied by the benefit level |
| Exhausted, delimited or relinquished | Any | No tuition is paid |
| Any (Chapter 30, Chapter 35 or Chapter 1606) | Any | No tuition is paid to the school |

**Yellow Ribbon matching** needs both parts: a tier eligible for it and a school agreement covering the program. A tier without eligibility, or a school without an agreement for the program, receives no matching.

**Hypothetical worked figures.** A private school charges $34000.00 net tuition and fees for the year; the student holds the 80% Benefit Level on an active record. The capped figure is $29920.95, and 80 percent of it is $23936.76. At a public school charging $9000.00 net in-state tuition and fees, the same student's school receives $7200.00.
